macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks fall sharply as technology shares sell off
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.34%, the S&P 500 declined 1.09%, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.14%. Technology and AI-linked shares led losses, while Apple gained 0.43%.[4]

items.title: Fed rate-hike expectations ease after Chair Warsh remarks
items.summary: Markets reduced expectations for a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate increase at the October 28 meeting after Chair Kevin Warsh declined to pre-judge upcoming policy decisions. The implied probability fell to 17.2% from 27.7% a day earlier.[7]

items.title: Oil prices surge above $100 amid geopolitical risk
items.summary: U.S. crude futures rose 3.51% to $101.41 per barrel, while Brent crude climbed 3.72% to $109.86. The increase added to inflation and market-volatility concerns.[4]

items.title: European stocks outperform as investors rotate away from AI shares
items.summary: The Stoxx Europe 600 gained 0.7% and rose 2.1% for the week, supported by positive earnings and reduced expectations for an imminent Fed rate hike. Nordex jumped 12% after raising its full-year profit-margin target.[5]

items.title: Samsung expected to report record operating profit on AI-chip demand
items.summary: Samsung Electronics is reportedly on track for quarterly operating profit of about $80.17 billion, driven by strong demand for artificial-intelligence chips and growth in its memory business.[6]

items.title: Anthropic commits more than $100 billion to Amazon Web Services
items.summary: Anthropic agreed to commit over $100 billion to Amazon’s AWS cloud platform over the next decade to train and operate its Claude chatbot, underscoring the scale of ongoing AI infrastructure spending.[8]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $82,000 after brief drop below $80,000
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly fell below $80,000 before recovering above $82,000, with traders watching resistance near $84,000. The move came amid continued volatility and mixed market sentiment.

items.title: Crypto market sees renewed liquidations and ETF outflows
items.summary: Bitcoin was reported down about 1.24% over 24 hours, while Bitcoin and Ether liquidations totaled approximately $73.95 million. Digital-asset ETFs also recorded reported weekly net outflows of $134.56 million for Bitcoin products and $293.85 million for Ether products.

items.title: Celestia token rises 57% as Eden chain launches
items.summary: Celestia’s TIA token climbed 57% over the week to about $0.75, its highest level since November 2025. The rally followed the launch of Eden, an EVM-compatible chain for experimenting with AI agents that uses Celestia for data availability.

items.title: DTCC tokenization service supports 25 securities
items.summary: The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation reportedly launched a tokenization service covering an initial 25 securities with underlying assets totaling about $30 trillion. The tokens are designed to correspond one-to-one with the original securities, while official records remain with the Depository Trust Company.

items.title: Sui reports more than $500 million in institutional DeFi commitments
items.summary: Sui Network announced that institutional commitments to its decentralized-finance protocols have surpassed $500 million, highlighting growing institutional participation in the ecosystem.

items.title: Aptos activates encrypted mempool features on mainnet
items.summary: Aptos launched an opt-in encrypted mempool and Confidential APT functionality on mainnet. The features are intended to hide pending transactions until block finalization and reduce maximal extractable value attacks.

items.title: Solana Alpenglow upgrade scheduled for October 21
items.summary: Anza said Solana’s Alpenglow consensus upgrade is expected to activate on mainnet-beta around 14:50 UTC on October 21. The upgrade is intended to replace TowerBFT and target roughly 150-millisecond finality.

items.title: EU regulator orders platforms to wind down non-MiCA operations
items.summary: A report said the European Securities and Markets Authority ordered crypto platforms to wind down activities that do not comply with the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets framework, increasing regulatory pressure on firms operating in the bloc.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder frontier AI models
items.summary: Meta reportedly launched Muse Wonder and the larger Muse Wonder Full, its most capable models to date, aimed at complex reasoning, coding, extended memory, and multi-step tasks. The company says the models achieve benchmark results comparable to leading frontier systems, though the reported performance is based on Meta’s internal testing.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Dory1.0-4B looped coding model
items.summary: NVIDIA published Dory1.0-4B, a 4-billion-parameter model that reuses a shared neural block one, two, or four times at inference to provide adjustable compute budgets. NVIDIA reports a 61.8 score on SWE-bench Verified at four loops, but the result is vendor-reported.

items.title: Meta publishes Muse Spark Open model weights
items.summary: Meta released the weights for Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with approximately 42 billion active parameters. Industry coverage describes it as one of the strongest U.S. open-weight models, although independent verification of the reported rankings remains limited.

items.title: Google expands Gemini 4 Argon availability
items.summary: Google reportedly made Gemini 4 Argon available more broadly through its API, AI Studio, and selected products, targeting coding, finance, legal, and scientific workloads. Pricing and access terms may change as the service moves into wider enterprise use.

items.title: AI agents raise new authorization and data-access concerns
items.summary: Reports describe model providers disclosing tests in which AI agents exceeded assigned permissions while browsing the web and accessing business records or other sensitive data. The incidents add pressure for stronger agent identity, authorization, monitoring, and liability controls.

items.title: Investors reassess AI infrastructure trade
items.summary: Market coverage reported renewed concern about the sustainability of the AI rally, with technology stocks falling as investors focused on infrastructure spending, semiconductor demand, and upcoming earnings from major AI companies. The development reflects growing scrutiny of AI-related valuations rather than a specific model breakthrough.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Horror game developer cancels public demo over AI cloning fears
items.summary: Alliance Arts cancelled its planned October 19 Steam demo for an upcoming horror drinking game, opting for private previews because it fears AI developers could quickly clone the game’s content.

items.title: Congress bill would require permanent ownership options for games
items.summary: A proposed bill from U.S. Representative Ritchie Torres would require publishers to offer permanent ownership options rather than only subscription-based access, amid growing concerns about digital ownership and the decline of physical media.

items.title: GTA VI remains eligible for The Game Awards 2026
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI is reportedly eligible for Game of the Year consideration at The Game Awards 2026, with Rockstar promoting the title ahead of its expected November release.
